columns.name: array_asset_name
columns.description: What `array_asset_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this array asset. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (Part 05 §8).

columns.name: semantic_type
columns.description: What quantity the asset holds, where the row's declared facts do not already say. Null is the ordinary case: a writer MUST NOT fill it where the device, the unit, the channel map or the dimensions carry the answer. An unrecognised value is a label carrying no contract (Part 01 §3.17).

columns.name: band
columns.description: Which band of a sampled signal this array holds: `wideband` unfiltered, `ap` the action-potential band, `lfp` the local field potential band, with Part 02 §9.3's meanings. A conventional shorthand for a filter the packet does not record. Null where the signal was not split.

columns.name: device_id
columns.description: The device that produced this array.

columns.name: processing_run_id
columns.description: The run that produced this array. Null means it was acquired rather than computed.

columns.name: unit
columns.description: The physical unit of the array's values, as a UCUM code.

columns.name: conversion
columns.description: Multiply stored values by this before offset.

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

columns.name: coordinate_position_column
columns.description: Which column of that resource holds the 0-based position.

columns.name: coordinate_resource
columns.description: The table whose rows are this axis's positions, as a dotted resource ID. The column of it holding the 0-based position is `coordinate_position_column`.

columns.name: coordinate_array_asset_id
columns.description: A 1-D array holding one value per position (irregular axis).

columns.name: coordinate_unit
columns.description: The physical unit of this axis's coordinate values, as a UCUM code.

columns.name: step_tick_den
columns.description: Denominator of the step, in ticks. Absent means 1.

columns.name: clock_id
columns.description: Clock the ticks are counted on (regular tick axis).

rules.message: an axis declares one half of its labelled coordinates; the resource says where the positions are and the column says which of its columns holds them
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index, coordinate_resource, coordinate_position_column FROM analysis.array_dimensions WHERE (coordinate_resource IS NULL) <> (coordinate_position_column IS NULL)

columns.name: t_tick
columns.description: Spike tick on clock_id, mapped through core.clock_anchors.

columns.name: clock_id
columns.description: The clock these ticks are on, normally the session's reference.

columns.name: time_bucket_tick
columns.description: First tick of the bucket this spike falls in, on clock_id.

rules.message: a spike precedes the start of the bucket it is labelled with
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, unit_id, t_tick, time_bucket_tick FROM analysis.spike_events WHERE time_bucket_tick > t_tick

rules.message: buckets overlap in tick range, so the layout they declare is not a partition
rules.sql: SELECT a.session_id, a.clock_id, a.time_bucket_tick AS earlier_bucket, a.hi, b.time_bucket_tick AS later_bucket, b.lo FROM (SELECT session_id, clock_id, time_bucket_tick, MIN(t_tick) AS lo, MAX(t_tick) AS hi FROM analysis.spike_events GROUP BY session_id, clock_id, time_bucket_tick) AS a JOIN (SELECT session_id, clock_id, time_bucket_tick, MIN(t_tick) AS lo, MAX(t_tick) AS hi FROM analysis.spike_events GROUP BY session_id, clock_id, time_bucket_tick) AS b ON a.session_id = b.session_id AND a.clock_id = b.clock_id AND b.time_bucket_tick > a.time_bucket_tick WHERE b.lo <= a.hi

columns.name: array_asset_name
columns.description: What `array_asset_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this array asset. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (Part 05 §8).

columns.name: semantic_type
columns.description: What quantity the asset holds, where the row's declared facts do not already say. Null is the ordinary case: a writer MUST NOT fill it where the device, the unit, the channel map or the dimensions carry the answer. An unrecognised value is a label carrying no contract (Part 01 §3.17).

columns.name: band
columns.description: Which band of a sampled signal this array holds: `wideband` unfiltered, `ap` the action-potential band, `lfp` the local field potential band, with Part 02 §9.3's meanings. A conventional shorthand for a filter the packet does not record. Null where the signal was not split.

columns.name: device_id
columns.description: The device that produced this array.

columns.name: processing_run_id
columns.description: The run that produced this array. Null means it was acquired rather than computed.

columns.name: unit
columns.description: The physical unit of the array's values, as a UCUM code.

columns.name: conversion
columns.description: Multiply stored values by this before offset.

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

rules.message: scaling is declared both on the array and per channel
rules.sql: SELECT a.array_asset_id FROM core.array_assets AS a WHERE a.conversion IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM core.array_channels AS c WHERE c.array_asset_id = a.array_asset_id AND c.conversion IS NOT NULL)

rules.message: sample_rate_hz disagrees with the time axis step
rules.sql: SELECT a.array_asset_id, a.sample_rate_hz FROM core.array_assets AS a JOIN core.array_dimensions AS d USING (array_asset_id) JOIN core.clocks AS c ON c.clock_id = d.clock_id WHERE a.sample_rate_hz IS NOT NULL AND CAST(d.step_tick_num AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / CAST(COALESCE(d.step_tick_den, 1) AS DOUBLE PRECISION) IS NOT NULL AND c.tick_rate_hz IS NOT NULL AND ABS(a.sample_rate_hz - CAST(c.tick_rate_hz AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / CAST(d.step_tick_num AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / CAST(COALESCE(d.step_tick_den, 1) AS DOUBLE PRECISION)) > 1e-6

columns.name: axis_index
columns.description: Axis that channel_index indexes, in stored order.

columns.name: inter_sample_shift
columns.description: Acquisition time offset within one sample period, in sample periods.

columns.name: unit
columns.description: The physical unit of the converted value, as a UCUM code.

columns.name: conversion
columns.description: Multiply stored values by this before offset.

rules.message: a conversion without a unit yields a number in no known quantity
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, channel_index FROM core.array_channels WHERE conversion IS NOT NULL AND unit IS NULL

columns.name: coordinate_position_column
columns.description: Which column of that resource holds the 0-based position.

columns.name: coordinate_resource
columns.description: The table whose rows are this axis's positions, as a dotted resource ID. The column of it holding the 0-based position is `coordinate_position_column`.

columns.name: coordinate_array_asset_id
columns.description: A 1-D array holding one value per position (irregular axis).

columns.name: coordinate_unit
columns.description: The physical unit of this axis's coordinate values, as a UCUM code.

columns.name: step_tick_den
columns.description: Denominator of the step, in ticks. Absent means 1.

columns.name: clock_id
columns.description: Clock the ticks are counted on (regular tick axis).

rules.message: axis_index is not contiguous from 0
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, COUNT(*) AS n_axes, MAX(axis_index) AS max_axis FROM core.array_dimensions GROUP BY array_asset_id HAVING MAX(axis_index) <> COUNT(*) - 1 OR MIN(axis_index) <> 0

rules.message: an axis declares more than one coordinate form
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index FROM core.array_dimensions WHERE (CASE WHEN origin_tick IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN origin_value IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN coordinate_array_asset_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN coordinate_resource IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 1

rules.message: a regular tick axis needs clock_id, origin_tick and step_tick_num
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index FROM core.array_dimensions WHERE origin_tick IS NOT NULL AND (step_tick_num IS NULL OR clock_id IS NULL)

rules.message: a regular numeric axis needs origin_value, step_value and coordinate_unit
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index FROM core.array_dimensions WHERE origin_value IS NOT NULL AND (step_value IS NULL OR coordinate_unit IS NULL)

rules.message: coordinate_resource and coordinate_position_column must be present together
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index FROM core.array_dimensions WHERE (coordinate_resource IS NULL) <> (coordinate_position_column IS NULL)

rules.message: a core axis points outward at a non-core resource
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index, coordinate_resource FROM core.array_dimensions WHERE coordinate_resource IS NOT NULL AND coordinate_resource NOT LIKE 'core.%'

rules.message: a step denominator is not positive, so the step it defines is meaningless
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index, step_tick_den FROM core.array_dimensions WHERE step_tick_den IS NOT NULL AND step_tick_den <= 0

rules.message: an axis declares one half of its labelled coordinates; the resource says where the positions are and the column says which of its columns holds them
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index, coordinate_resource, coordinate_position_column FROM core.array_dimensions WHERE (coordinate_resource IS NULL) <> (coordinate_position_column IS NULL)

columns.name: calibration_id
columns.description: The calibration this row names a device for.

columns.name: calibration_id
columns.description: The calibration this point belongs to.

columns.name: point_index
columns.description: 0-based position in the curve's own order. The key is not `input_value` even though the inputs are distinct: an equality join on a float64 is not safe, so the key uses an explicit sequence position.

columns.name: input_value
columns.description: The setting the point was measured at.

columns.name: calibration_name
columns.description: What `calibration_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this calibration. Required, and composed by the writer where the source names none, since Part 02 §8.2 makes two calibrations sharing a name one row.

columns.name: calibration_type
columns.description: What was calibrated: `water_volume`, `light_power`, `manipulator_transform`. Named `_type` rather than `_kind` because a `_kind` column is a discriminator (Part 02 §8.3), and this holds a value that resolves to no table.

columns.name: calibrated_at
columns.description: When the calibration was measured, which is not when it was in force; measured examples differ by 133 and 302 days. Null where the source states none, since what a source did not say is not invented (Part 01 §3.5).

columns.name: description
columns.description: What the source said the calibration was.

columns.name: input_unit
columns.description: The unit of `core.calibration_points.input_value`, as a UCUM code. On the calibration because it varies per calibration -- `s` for water, `V` for opto -- so no literal unit can sit on the value column.

columns.name: output_unit
columns.description: The unit of `core.calibration_points.output_value`, as a UCUM code.

columns.name: array_asset_id
columns.description: The array holding this calibration where its content is one rather than a curve: a manipulator transform, a camera's intrinsics.

columns.name: detail_kind
columns.description: A table carrying a calibration shape core does not define, as a dotted resource ID. A kind the packet cannot resolve records that the content is elsewhere rather than that the row is wrong (Part 02 §12.3).

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

rules.message: a calibration declares one unit of measure and not the other; the pair is what makes a point readable
rules.sql: SELECT calibration_id, input_unit, output_unit FROM core.calibrations WHERE (input_unit IS NULL) <> (output_unit IS NULL)

rules.message: a calibration carries points and declares no units, so nothing says what its values are measured in
rules.sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.calibration_id FROM core.calibrations AS c JOIN core.calibration_points AS p USING (calibration_id) WHERE c.input_unit IS NULL OR c.output_unit IS NULL

columns.name: anchor_index
columns.description: 0-based position in this clock's anchor sequence.

rules.message: anchors are declared for a clock with no parent
rules.sql: SELECT DISTINCT a.clock_id FROM core.clock_anchors AS a JOIN core.clocks AS c USING (clock_id) WHERE c.parent_clock_id IS NULL

rules.message: anchor_index is not contiguous from 0
rules.sql: SELECT clock_id, COUNT(*) AS n, MAX(anchor_index) AS hi FROM core.clock_anchors GROUP BY clock_id HAVING MAX(anchor_index) <> COUNT(*) - 1 OR MIN(anchor_index) <> 0

rules.message: anchor sequences do not increase together, so interpolation is undefined
rules.sql: SELECT clock_id, anchor_index FROM (SELECT *, LAG(t_tick) OVER (PARTITION BY clock_id ORDER BY anchor_index) AS prev_t, LAG(parent_tick) OVER (PARTITION BY clock_id ORDER BY anchor_index) AS prev_p FROM core.clock_anchors) AS derived_1 WHERE prev_t IS NOT NULL AND (t_tick <= prev_t OR parent_tick <= prev_p)

rules.message: an anchor gap exceeds twice the median, leaving ticks the mapping does not define
rules.sql: WITH gaps AS (SELECT clock_id, anchor_index, CAST(t_tick AS DECIMAL(38,0)) - CAST(LAG(t_tick) OVER (PARTITION BY clock_id ORDER BY anchor_index) AS DECIMAL(38,0)) AS gap FROM core.clock_anchors), typical AS (SELECT clock_id, PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY gap) AS m FROM gaps WHERE gap IS NOT NULL GROUP BY clock_id) SELECT g.clock_id, g.anchor_index, g.gap, t.m FROM gaps AS g JOIN typical AS t USING (clock_id) WHERE g.gap IS NOT NULL AND g.gap > t.m * 2

rules.message: stop_tick precedes start_tick
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, clock_id, start_tick, stop_tick FROM core.clock_observation_intervals WHERE stop_tick < start_tick

rules.message: observation windows overlap, which would double-count observed time
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, clock_id, start_tick, stop_tick FROM (SELECT *, LAG(stop_tick) OVER (PARTITION BY session_id, clock_id ORDER BY start_tick) AS prev_stop FROM core.clock_observation_intervals) AS checked_interval WHERE prev_stop IS NOT NULL AND start_tick <= prev_stop

columns.name: parent_tick
columns.description: The same instant on the parent clock.

columns.name: shift_seconds
columns.description: How far the parent's phase moved. Signed.

columns.name: anchor_interval_span
columns.description: How many consecutive anchor intervals the step spans.

rules.message: a phase step is recorded on a clock with no parent, and a step is a movement of the parent's phase
rules.sql: SELECT s.session_id, s.clock_id, s.t_tick FROM core.clock_phase_steps AS s JOIN core.clocks AS c ON c.session_id = s.session_id AND c.clock_id = s.clock_id WHERE c.parent_clock_id IS NULL

columns.name: clock_name
columns.description: What `clock_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this clock. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (Part 05 §8).

columns.name: tick_rate_hz
columns.description: Tick rate as float, required unless exact tick rate provided.

columns.name: origin
columns.description: Where this clock's tick 0 is, in the source's own terms -- for a sample clock, tick 0 is sample 0, and a writer MUST NOT re-base a source's index (Part 01 §2.2).

columns.name: tick_zero_utc
columns.description: Wall-clock instant of tick 0 on this clock.

columns.name: transform_slope
columns.description: Parent ticks per this clock's tick, as measured.

columns.name: transform_offset
columns.description: Parent-clock tick at this clock's tick 0.

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

columns.name: withheld_first_anchor
columns.description: Whether Part 02 §12.6's terminal-anchor test withheld this clock's first anchor. Null means the test did not run.

columns.name: withheld_last_anchor
columns.description: Whether Part 02 §12.6's terminal-anchor test withheld this clock's last anchor. Null means the test did not run.

rules.message: neither tick_rate_hz nor an exact rational rate is present
rules.sql: SELECT clock_id FROM core.clocks WHERE tick_rate_hz IS NULL AND (tick_rate_num IS NULL OR tick_rate_den IS NULL)

rules.message: a clock declares both a float rate and a rational one
rules.sql: SELECT clock_id, tick_rate_hz, tick_rate_num, tick_rate_den FROM core.clocks WHERE tick_rate_hz IS NOT NULL AND tick_rate_num IS NOT NULL

rules.message: tick rate is not positive
rules.sql: SELECT clock_id, tick_rate_hz, tick_rate_num, tick_rate_den FROM core.clocks WHERE tick_rate_hz <= 0 OR tick_rate_num <= 0 OR tick_rate_den <= 0

rules.message: transform_slope and transform_offset must be present together
rules.sql: SELECT clock_id FROM core.clocks WHERE (transform_slope IS NULL) <> (transform_offset IS NULL)

rules.message: a clock transform is declared without a parent clock
rules.sql: SELECT clock_id FROM core.clocks WHERE parent_clock_id IS NULL AND transform_slope IS NOT NULL

rules.message: tick_zero_utc is more than a day from session_start_time
rules.sql: SELECT c.clock_id, c.tick_zero_utc, s.session_start_time FROM core.clocks AS c JOIN core.sessions AS s USING (session_id) WHERE c.tick_zero_utc IS NOT NULL AND s.session_start_time IS NOT NULL AND (c.tick_zero_utc < s.session_start_time - INTERVAL '1' DAY OR c.tick_zero_utc > s.session_start_time + INTERVAL '1' DAY)

rules.message: a clock declares both a linear transform and anchor points
rules.sql: SELECT c.clock_id FROM core.clocks AS c WHERE c.transform_slope IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM core.clock_anchors AS a WHERE a.clock_id = c.clock_id)

rules.message: a clock is its own ancestor, so walking the chain does not terminate
rules.sql: WITH RECURSIVE up(clock_id, ancestor, depth) AS (SELECT clock_id, parent_clock_id, 1 FROM core.clocks WHERE parent_clock_id IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT u.clock_id, c.parent_clock_id, u.depth + 1 FROM up AS u JOIN core.clocks AS c ON c.clock_id = u.ancestor WHERE c.parent_clock_id IS NOT NULL AND u.depth < 64) SELECT DISTINCT clock_id FROM up WHERE ancestor = clock_id OR depth >= 64

rules.message: a non-reference clock declares no alignment, so it cannot be converted
rules.sql: SELECT c.clock_id FROM core.clocks AS c JOIN core.sessions AS s USING (session_id) WHERE s.reference_clock_id IS NOT NULL AND c.clock_id <> s.reference_clock_id AND c.transform_slope IS NULL AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM core.clock_anchors AS a WHERE a.clock_id = c.clock_id)

rules.message: a clock that is anchored or is the session's reference declares no observation interval, so nothing on it has a window to inherit
rules.sql: SELECT c.session_id, c.clock_id FROM core.clocks AS c LEFT JOIN core.clock_observation_intervals AS o ON o.session_id = c.session_id AND o.clock_id = c.clock_id WHERE o.clock_id IS NULL AND (EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM core.clock_anchors AS a WHERE a.session_id = c.session_id AND a.clock_id = c.clock_id) OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM core.sessions AS s WHERE s.session_id = c.session_id AND s.reference_clock_id = c.clock_id))

rules.message: a clock with no anchors records the outcome of a terminal-anchor test that cannot have run on it
rules.sql: SELECT c.session_id, c.clock_id FROM core.clocks AS c WHERE (c.withheld_first_anchor IS NOT NULL OR c.withheld_last_anchor IS NOT NULL) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM core.clock_anchors AS a WHERE a.session_id = c.session_id AND a.clock_id = c.clock_id)

columns.name: coordinate_frame
columns.description: The frame these axes belong to.

columns.name: axis_name
columns.description: Whatever the source called the field these values came from, verbatim (Part 02 §9.3). A writer MUST NOT normalise it or replace it with what the quantity is conventionally taken to be.

columns.name: axis_direction
columns.description: Which way the values increase -- `right`, `anterior`, `superior`. Null where the source does not state it, which no inference may fill.

columns.name: unit
columns.description: The axis's unit, as a UCUM code (Part 02 §8.4).

rules.message: two axes of one frame name the same field, so which axis a coordinate value sits on cannot be told
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, coordinate_frame, axis_name, COUNT(*) AS axes FROM core.coordinate_frame_axes GROUP BY session_id, coordinate_frame, axis_name HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

columns.name: coordinate_frame
columns.description: The session's own name for this space.

columns.name: atlas
columns.description: The published atlas this space is, where it is one. Null where no source names it; a writer MUST NOT read one out of the frame's name.

columns.name: atlas_version
columns.description: That atlas's version, spelled as the atlas spells it -- `CCFv3`. Two packets naming one atlas at different versions are in different spaces.

columns.name: description
columns.description: What the frame is, for a reader without the atlas.

columns.name: curation_name
columns.description: What `curation_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this curation. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (Part 05 §8).

columns.name: processing_run_id
columns.description: The run that produced this record, where provenance is recorded.

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

columns.name: session_id
columns.description: Session if device record is session-scoped.

columns.name: device_name
columns.description: What `device_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this device. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (Part 05 §8).

columns.name: manufacturer
columns.description: The manufacturer's own name for itself, as the source states it, compared exactly, so two spellings are two manufacturers.

columns.name: firmware_version
columns.description: The firmware the instrument was running, verbatim as its source stated it.

columns.name: hardware_version
columns.description: The instrument's hardware revision, verbatim as its source stated it.

columns.name: parent_device_id
columns.description: The device this one was attached to -- a probe's headstage, a headstage's connect board. Null at the root of a chain, or where no source states it.

columns.name: parent_port
columns.description: Which port, dock or slot of `parent_device_id` this device attached to. Null where the attachment is stated and its coordinate is not. Establishes nothing about identity: two rows may share a parent and a port (Part 01 §3.5).

columns.name: device_kind
columns.description: The table carrying this device's kind-specific facts, as a dotted resource ID. Its primary key begins `device_id`, so resolution is Part 02 §8.3's shared-key join. Core declares no such table (Part 02 §8.3); an extension does, and a value naming a resource the packet does not carry is a fact rather than a defect (Part 02 §8.3).

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

rules.message: a device is its own ancestor, or its attachment chain does not terminate
rules.sql: WITH RECURSIVE up(device_id, ancestor, depth) AS (SELECT device_id, parent_device_id, 1 FROM core.devices WHERE parent_device_id IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT u.device_id, d.parent_device_id, u.depth + 1 FROM up AS u JOIN core.devices AS d ON d.device_id = u.ancestor WHERE d.parent_device_id IS NOT NULL AND u.depth < 64) SELECT DISTINCT device_id FROM up WHERE ancestor = device_id OR depth >= 64

rules.message: one serial number appears on more than one device row; a device is the physical object
rules.sql: SELECT serial_number, COUNT(*) AS n_rows FROM core.devices WHERE serial_number IS NOT NULL GROUP BY serial_number HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

columns.name: coordinate_frame
columns.description: The frame, naming a `core.coordinate_frames` row of this session; with `coordinate_basis` it completes the parent's key.

columns.name: axis_index
columns.description: Which of the frame's axes this value is on.

columns.name: axis_value
columns.description: The value, in the axis's unit.

columns.name: coordinate_frame
columns.description: The space these coordinates are in, naming a `core.coordinate_frames` row of this session, which declares that space's axes and the published atlas it is.

columns.name: coordinate_basis
columns.description: What the coordinate asserts: `planned` where the probe was meant to go, `measured` where it was, `nominal` where it is by construction and nothing aimed or observed it (Part 01 §3.8). A consumer that does not recognise a basis MUST NOT treat it as measured (Part 01 §3.8).

columns.name: region_id
columns.description: The atlas structure this position falls in, numbered by the atlas that `coordinate_frame` names.

columns.name: region_label
columns.description: That structure's short name, so a consumer without the atlas can read the annotation.

columns.name: processing_run_id
columns.description: The run that produced this coordinate.

columns.name: electrode_name
columns.description: What `electrode_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this electrode. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (Part 05 §8).

columns.name: local_electrode_label
columns.description: Opaque source label; undefined base, not an offset.

columns.name: local_channel_label
columns.description: Opaque source label; undefined base, not an offset.

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

columns.name: start_tick
columns.description: First observed tick, on the stream's clock.

columns.name: stop_tick
columns.description: Last observed tick, on the stream's clock.

rules.message: stop_tick precedes start_tick
rules.sql: SELECT event_stream_id, start_tick, stop_tick FROM core.event_stream_observation_intervals WHERE stop_tick < start_tick

rules.message: observation windows overlap, which would double-count observed time
rules.sql: SELECT event_stream_id, start_tick, stop_tick FROM (SELECT *, LAG(stop_tick) OVER (PARTITION BY event_stream_id ORDER BY start_tick) AS prev_stop FROM core.event_stream_observation_intervals) AS checked_interval WHERE prev_stop IS NOT NULL AND start_tick <= prev_stop

columns.name: event_stream_name
columns.description: What `event_stream_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this event stream. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (Part 05 §8).

columns.name: event_type
columns.description: What kind of event this stream emits. A stream emits one kind, so a source emitting several on one channel is written as several streams.

columns.name: detail_kind
columns.description: A table specialising this stream's events, as a dotted resource ID. A kind the packet cannot resolve records that the detail is elsewhere (Part 02 §8.3). Resolved against `core.events`' key by Part 02 §8.3's shared key, through the reference `discriminates_via` names.

columns.name: device_id
columns.description: The device that produced it, where one is identified.

columns.name: clock_id
columns.description: The clock its events are timed on.

columns.name: processing_run_id
columns.description: The run that produced it. Null means it came off the device as recorded. The manifest records outputs per resource and cannot distinguish streams within one table.

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

rules.message: streams carry no observation intervals and their clock declares none, so no rate over them has a denominator
rules.sql: SELECT s.event_stream_id, s.event_stream_name FROM core.event_streams AS s WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM core.event_stream_observation_intervals AS o WHERE o.event_stream_id = s.event_stream_id) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM core.clock_observation_intervals AS c WHERE c.session_id = s.session_id AND c.clock_id = s.clock_id)

columns.name: stream_id
columns.description: The stream this event belongs to.

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

rules.message: events fall outside the observation window in force for their stream
rules.sql: WITH stream_windows AS (SELECT o.event_stream_id, o.start_tick, o.stop_tick FROM core.event_stream_observation_intervals AS o UNION ALL SELECT s.event_stream_id, c.start_tick, c.stop_tick FROM core.event_streams AS s JOIN core.clock_observation_intervals AS c ON c.session_id = s.session_id AND c.clock_id = s.clock_id WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM core.event_stream_observation_intervals AS o WHERE o.event_stream_id = s.event_stream_id)), observed AS (SELECT DISTINCT event_stream_id FROM stream_windows) SELECT e.session_id, e.stream_id, e.t_tick FROM core.events AS e JOIN observed AS k ON e.stream_id = k.event_stream_id LEFT JOIN stream_windows AS w ON e.stream_id = w.event_stream_id AND e.t_tick BETWEEN w.start_tick AND w.stop_tick WHERE w.start_tick IS NULL

columns.name: interval_kind
columns.description: The resource that specialises this interval, as a dotted resource ID, resolved as Part 02 §8.3's shared key.

columns.name: start_tick
columns.description: First tick of the trial, inclusive, on `clock_id`.

columns.name: stop_tick
columns.description: Last tick of the trial, inclusive, on `clock_id`.

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

rules.message: stop_tick precedes start_tick
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, interval_kind, interval_id, start_tick, stop_tick FROM core.intervals WHERE stop_tick < start_tick

columns.name: media_asset_name
columns.description: What `media_asset_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this media asset. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (Part 05 §8).

columns.name: semantic_type
columns.description: What quantity the asset holds, where the row's declared facts do not already say. Null is the ordinary case: a writer MUST NOT fill it where the device, the unit, the channel map or the dimensions carry the answer. An unrecognised value is a label carrying no contract (Part 01 §3.17).

columns.name: format
columns.description: The container format, as the file extension names it: `mp4`, `avi`.

columns.name: device_id
columns.description: The device that recorded this asset. A writer names it where its source states one, and MUST NOT infer it from a file name (Part 01 §3.5).

columns.name: pts_rate_num
columns.description: Presentation timestamps per second in this asset's container: numerator.

columns.name: pts_rate_den
columns.description: Presentation timestamps per second in this asset's container: denominator.

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

rules.message: an asset declares one half of its presentation-timestamp rate; half a rational is unusable
rules.sql: SELECT media_asset_id, pts_rate_num, pts_rate_den FROM core.media_assets WHERE (pts_rate_num IS NULL) <> (pts_rate_den IS NULL)

rules.message: frames carry pts for an asset that does not say what those timestamps count
rules.sql: SELECT a.media_asset_id FROM core.media_assets AS a WHERE a.pts_rate_num IS NULL AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM core.media_frames AS f WHERE f.media_asset_id = a.media_asset_id AND f.pts IS NOT NULL)

rules.message: a presentation-timestamp rate is not positive
rules.sql: SELECT media_asset_id, pts_rate_num, pts_rate_den FROM core.media_assets WHERE pts_rate_num <= 0 OR pts_rate_den <= 0

columns.name: pts
columns.description: Container presentation timestamp, verbatim in the container's own time base.

rules.message: frame_index is not contiguous from 0 within an asset
rules.sql: SELECT media_asset_id, COUNT(*) AS n_frames, MAX(frame_index) AS max_index FROM core.media_frames GROUP BY media_asset_id HAVING MAX(frame_index) <> COUNT(*) - 1 OR MIN(frame_index) <> 0

rules.message: pts is not strictly increasing in frame_index order within an asset, so the frames are not numbered in presentation order
rules.sql: SELECT media_asset_id, frame_index, pts, prev AS previous_pts FROM (SELECT media_asset_id, frame_index, pts, LAG(pts) OVER (PARTITION BY media_asset_id ORDER BY frame_index) AS prev FROM core.media_frames WHERE pts IS NOT NULL) AS derived_1 WHERE prev IS NOT NULL AND pts <= prev

columns.name: activity_type
columns.description: Which kind of output this preference is about, in the vocabulary `core.processing_runs.activity_type` uses (Part 02 §9.3).

columns.name: scope_kind
columns.description: The resource whose primary key `scope` holds, as a dotted resource ID.

columns.name: scope
columns.description: What it applies to -- a probe_id, an array_asset_id, a camera -- or the session_id itself where the preference is session-wide.

rules.message: a preference names a run whose activity_type differs from the preference's
rules.sql: SELECT p.session_id, p.activity_type AS preferred_activity_type, p.scope, r.activity_type AS run_activity_type FROM core.preferred_runs AS p JOIN core.processing_runs AS r USING (processing_run_id) WHERE r.activity_type IS DISTINCT FROM p.activity_type

rules.message: a preference names a run belonging to another session
rules.sql: SELECT p.session_id AS preferred_session_id, p.processing_run_id, r.session_id AS run_session_id FROM core.preferred_runs AS p JOIN core.processing_runs AS r USING (processing_run_id) WHERE r.session_id IS NOT NULL AND r.session_id IS DISTINCT FROM p.session_id

rules.message: the preferred run is superseded by another run
rules.sql: SELECT p.session_id, p.activity_type, p.scope, p.processing_run_id FROM core.preferred_runs AS p WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM core.processing_runs AS r WHERE r.supersedes_run_id = p.processing_run_id)

columns.name: probe_name
columns.description: What `probe_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this probe. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (Part 05 §8).

columns.name: probe_type
columns.description: The probe's model, as the manufacturer names it: `Neuropixels 1.0`.

columns.name: manufacturer
columns.description: The manufacturer's own name for itself, as the source states it, compared exactly, so two spellings are two manufacturers.

columns.name: target_region
columns.description: The structure the probe was aimed at, as an atlas acronym where the source gives one. Not resolvable: no column here names the atlas, which only a coordinate frame does (Part 01 §3.24).

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

columns.name: source_file_id
columns.description: A source file the run consumed.

columns.name: processing_run_name
columns.description: What `processing_run_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this processing run. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (Part 05 §8).

columns.name: activity_type
columns.description: What kind of work the run did: `import`, `validation`, `sorting`, `curation`, `materialization`. A pipeline names its own.

columns.name: scope
columns.description: What this run is about -- a probe_id, an array_asset_id, a camera -- or the session_id itself where the run is session-wide. Read only with the `scope_kind` beside it, which names the table the value keys into.

columns.name: scope_kind
columns.description: The resource whose primary key `scope` holds, as a dotted resource ID -- `core.probes`, `core.array_assets`. A value naming no declared resource means the scope is not a packet resource. Set with `scope` or not at all.

columns.name: supersedes_run_id
columns.description: The run this one replaces, if any.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Whether the run completed, with the meanings Part 02 §9.3 declares.

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

rules.message: a failed run is recorded in a committed packet
rules.sql: SELECT processing_run_id, activity_type FROM core.processing_runs WHERE status = 'failed'

rules.message: a materialization run does not record the software that produced it
rules.sql: SELECT processing_run_id, software_name, software_version FROM core.processing_runs WHERE activity_type = 'materialization' AND (software_name IS NULL OR software_version IS NULL)

rules.message: a run supersedes_run_id itself
rules.sql: SELECT processing_run_id FROM core.processing_runs WHERE supersedes_run_id = processing_run_id

rules.message: the supersedes chain contains a cycle
rules.sql: WITH RECURSIVE up(processing_run_id, ancestor, depth) AS (SELECT processing_run_id, supersedes_run_id, 1 FROM core.processing_runs WHERE supersedes_run_id IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT u.processing_run_id, r.supersedes_run_id, u.depth + 1 FROM up AS u JOIN core.processing_runs AS r ON r.processing_run_id = u.ancestor WHERE r.supersedes_run_id IS NOT NULL AND u.depth < 64) SELECT DISTINCT processing_run_id FROM up WHERE ancestor = processing_run_id OR depth >= 64

rules.message: several runs share an activity and scope and none is preferred, so a consumer cannot choose between them
rules.sql: WITH grouped AS (SELECT session_id, activity_type, scope, COUNT(*) AS n FROM core.processing_runs WHERE scope IS NOT NULL GROUP BY session_id, activity_type, scope HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) SELECT g.session_id, g.activity_type, g.scope, g.n FROM grouped AS g WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM core.preferred_runs AS p WHERE p.activity_type = g.activity_type AND p.scope = g.scope AND (p.session_id = g.session_id OR (p.session_id IS NULL AND g.session_id IS NULL)))

rules.message: an activity has several runs and at least one records no scope, so whether they compete cannot be determined
rules.sql: WITH per_activity AS (SELECT session_id, activity_type, COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE scope IS NULL) AS unscoped FROM core.processing_runs GROUP BY session_id, activity_type) SELECT session_id, activity_type, n, unscoped FROM per_activity WHERE n > 1 AND unscoped > 0

rules.message: a run declares one half of its scope; the pair is what carries the meaning
rules.sql: SELECT processing_run_id, scope_kind, scope FROM core.processing_runs WHERE (scope IS NULL) <> (scope_kind IS NULL)

columns.name: session_name
columns.description: What `session_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this session. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (Part 05 §8).

columns.name: session_start_time
columns.description: Session start time if known; if unknown use explicit null only in non-strict test packets.

columns.name: session_end_time
columns.description: When the session ended, UTC. Metadata, not derived from the tables.

columns.name: reference_clock_id
columns.description: The clock this session's times are reported on by default.

columns.name: t_zero_tick
columns.description: Earliest observed tick, on `reference_clock_id`; the origin seconds count from.

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

columns.name: alignment_bound
columns.description: How far past its anchors the writer mapped, in median anchor intervals (Part 01 §3.9). Null means the default of one.

rules.message: session_end_time precedes session_start_time
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, session_start_time, session_end_time FROM core.sessions WHERE session_end_time < session_start_time

rules.message: a session declaring more than one clock names no reference clock
rules.sql: SELECT s.session_id, COUNT(*) AS n_clocks FROM core.sessions AS s JOIN core.clocks AS c USING (session_id) WHERE s.reference_clock_id IS NULL GROUP BY s.session_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

rules.message: a clock does not reach the session's reference clock, so it cannot be converted to it
rules.sql: WITH RECURSIVE up(clock_id, ancestor, depth) AS (SELECT clock_id, clock_id, 0 FROM core.clocks UNION ALL SELECT u.clock_id, c.parent_clock_id, u.depth + 1 FROM up AS u JOIN core.clocks AS c ON c.clock_id = u.ancestor WHERE c.parent_clock_id IS NOT NULL AND u.depth < 64) SELECT c.session_id, c.clock_id FROM core.clocks AS c JOIN core.sessions AS s USING (session_id) WHERE s.reference_clock_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM up AS u WHERE u.clock_id = c.clock_id AND u.ancestor = s.reference_clock_id)

rules.message: a session declares an alignment bound below the default of one median anchor interval, which reaches no further than declaring nothing
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, alignment_bound FROM core.sessions WHERE alignment_bound < 1.0

columns.name: sorting_run_id
columns.description: The run whose channel list this row belongs to.

columns.name: channel_index
columns.description: 0-based position in the run's own channel order, which is what a source's channel index counts. int64 as every structural index is.

rules.message: a contact appears more than once in one run's channel list
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, sorting_run_id, electrode_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM core.sorting_run_channels GROUP BY session_id, sorting_run_id, electrode_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

rules.message: channel_index is not contiguous from 0 within a run
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, sorting_run_id, COUNT(*) AS n, MAX(channel_index) AS hi FROM core.sorting_run_channels GROUP BY session_id, sorting_run_id HAVING MAX(channel_index) <> COUNT(*) - 1 OR MIN(channel_index) <> 0

columns.name: sorting_run_name
columns.description: What `sorting_run_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this sorting run. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (Part 05 §8).

columns.name: processing_run_id
columns.description: The run that produced this record, where provenance is recorded.

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

columns.name: source_file_name
columns.description: What `source_file_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this source file. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (Part 05 §8).

columns.name: format
columns.description: The file's format in the producer's own terms, which this specification does not constrain.

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

rules.message: negative ticks on a clock with no absolute reference
rules.sql: SELECT u.session_id, u.clock_id, MIN(s.t_tick) AS min_tick FROM core.spike_events AS s JOIN core.units AS u USING (unit_id) JOIN core.clocks AS c ON c.clock_id = u.clock_id WHERE s.t_tick < 0 AND c.tick_zero_utc IS NULL GROUP BY u.session_id, u.clock_id

rules.message: spikes fall outside the observation window in force for their unit
rules.sql: WITH unit_windows AS (SELECT o.unit_id, o.start_tick, o.stop_tick FROM core.unit_observation_intervals AS o UNION ALL SELECT u.unit_id, c.start_tick, c.stop_tick FROM core.units AS u JOIN core.clock_observation_intervals AS c ON c.session_id = u.session_id AND c.clock_id = u.clock_id WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM core.unit_observation_intervals AS o WHERE o.unit_id = u.unit_id)), observed AS (SELECT DISTINCT unit_id FROM unit_windows) SELECT s.session_id, s.unit_id, s.t_tick FROM core.spike_events AS s JOIN observed AS k ON s.unit_id = k.unit_id LEFT JOIN unit_windows AS w ON s.unit_id = w.unit_id AND s.t_tick BETWEEN w.start_tick AND w.stop_tick WHERE w.start_tick IS NULL

columns.name: subject_name
columns.description: What `subject_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this subject. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (Part 05 §8).

columns.name: species
columns.description: The scientific name of the organism the subject derives from, as NCBI Taxonomy spells it: `Mus musculus`, never `mouse`. Null where the subject derives from no organism -- Part 01 §3.4 admits a preparation, and a phantom or a simulation has no species.

columns.name: strain
columns.description: The strain in its registry's nomenclature: MGI for mouse, where `C57BL/6J`'s substrain letter is what distinguishes it from the Nnt-deleted `C57BL/6N`, and RGD for rat stocks such as `Long-Evans`.

columns.name: sex
columns.description: The subject's sex. Null where the source states none, states it unknown, or describes a preparation that has none.

columns.name: genotype
columns.description: The genotype as the source states it, in MGI allele nomenclature where it uses one.

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

columns.name: coordinate_frame
columns.description: The frame, naming a `core.coordinate_frames` row of this session; with `coordinate_basis` it completes the parent's key.

columns.name: axis_index
columns.description: Which of the frame's axes this value is on.

columns.name: axis_value
columns.description: The value, in the axis's unit.

columns.name: coordinate_frame
columns.description: The space these coordinates are in, naming a `core.coordinate_frames` row of this session, which declares that space's axes and the published atlas it is.

columns.name: coordinate_basis
columns.description: What the coordinate asserts: `planned` where the probe was meant to go, `measured` where it was, `nominal` where it is by construction and nothing aimed or observed it (Part 01 §3.8). A consumer that does not recognise a basis MUST NOT treat it as measured (Part 01 §3.8).

columns.name: region_id
columns.description: The atlas structure this position falls in, numbered by the atlas that `coordinate_frame` names.

columns.name: region_label
columns.description: That structure's short name, so a consumer without the atlas can read the annotation.

columns.name: processing_run_id
columns.description: The run that produced this coordinate.

columns.name: electrode_id
columns.description: An electrode this unit was detected on.

columns.name: channel_index
columns.description: 0-based position of this electrode in the unit's channel list, where a dense array axis is indexed by it. Nothing joins on it.

columns.name: is_primary
columns.description: Whether this is the unit's peak electrode.

rules.message: a unit designates more than one peak electrode
rules.sql: SELECT unit_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM core.unit_electrodes WHERE is_primary GROUP BY unit_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

rules.message: channel_index is not contiguous from 0, so a dense axis indexed by it addresses rows that are not there
rules.sql: SELECT unit_id, COUNT(*) AS n, MAX(channel_index) AS hi FROM core.unit_electrodes WHERE channel_index IS NOT NULL GROUP BY unit_id HAVING MAX(channel_index) <> COUNT(*) - 1 OR MIN(channel_index) <> 0

rules.message: a unit sits on an electrode its sorting run did not use
rules.sql: SELECT ue.unit_id, ue.electrode_id FROM core.unit_electrodes AS ue JOIN core.units AS u ON ue.unit_id = u.unit_id JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT session_id, sorting_run_id FROM core.sorting_run_channels) AS d ON d.session_id = u.session_id AND d.sorting_run_id = u.sorting_run_id LEFT JOIN core.sorting_run_channels AS c ON c.session_id = u.session_id AND c.sorting_run_id = u.sorting_run_id AND c.electrode_id = ue.electrode_id WHERE c.electrode_id IS NULL

rules.message: stop_tick precedes start_tick
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, unit_id, start_tick, stop_tick FROM core.unit_observation_intervals WHERE stop_tick < start_tick

rules.message: observation windows overlap, which would double-count observed time
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, unit_id, start_tick, stop_tick FROM (SELECT *, LAG(stop_tick) OVER (PARTITION BY session_id, unit_id ORDER BY start_tick) AS prev_stop FROM core.unit_observation_intervals) AS checked_interval WHERE prev_stop IS NOT NULL AND start_tick <= prev_stop

columns.name: source
columns.description: What produced the label, e.g. kilosort, decoder, bombcell.

columns.name: normalized_label
columns.description: Declared projection onto the closed set. Null where the source's label does not project.

columns.name: confidence
columns.description: The source's confidence, where it reports one.

rules.message: a (source, label) pair projects onto more than one normalized_label
rules.sql: SELECT source, label, COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(normalized_label, '')) AS distinct_projections FROM core.unit_quality_labels GROUP BY source, label HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(normalized_label, '')) > 1

columns.name: unit_name
columns.description: What `unit_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this unit. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (Part 05 §8).

columns.name: local_unit_label
columns.description: Opaque source label; undefined base, not an offset.

columns.name: amplitude_unit
columns.description: Unit of measure of `core.spike_events.amplitude` for this unit's spikes -- microvolts, or ADC counts.

columns.name: quality_label_source
columns.description: Which core.unit_quality_labels source the designated label came from.

columns.name: n_spikes
columns.description: Total spikes for this unit in this context.

columns.name: clock_id
columns.description: The clock every tick of this unit is counted on.

columns.name: metadata
columns.description: What the source stated about this row that the standard does not model, carried in the source's own vocabulary and read by no rule.

rules.message: n_spikes, first_spike_tick or last_spike_tick disagrees with core.spike_events
rules.sql: SELECT u.session_id, u.unit_id FROM core.units AS u LEFT JOIN (SELECT unit_id, COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(t_tick) AS lo, MAX(t_tick) AS hi FROM core.spike_events GROUP BY unit_id) AS s USING (unit_id) WHERE (u.n_spikes IS NOT NULL AND u.n_spikes IS DISTINCT FROM COALESCE(s.n, 0)) OR (u.first_spike_tick IS NOT NULL AND u.first_spike_tick IS DISTINCT FROM s.lo) OR (u.last_spike_tick IS NOT NULL AND u.last_spike_tick IS DISTINCT FROM s.hi)

rules.message: the designated quality label is not among the recorded ones
rules.sql: SELECT u.session_id, u.unit_id, u.quality_label, u.quality_label_source FROM core.units AS u LEFT JOIN core.unit_quality_labels AS q ON u.unit_id = q.unit_id AND u.quality_label = q.normalized_label AND u.quality_label_source = q.source WHERE u.quality_label IS NOT NULL AND q.source IS NULL

rules.message: quality_label and quality_label_source must be present together
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, unit_id FROM core.units WHERE (quality_label IS NULL) <> (quality_label_source IS NULL)

rules.message: units carry no observation intervals and their clock declares none, so no rate over them has a denominator
rules.sql: SELECT u.session_id, u.unit_id FROM core.units AS u WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM core.unit_observation_intervals AS o WHERE o.unit_id = u.unit_id) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM core.clock_observation_intervals AS c WHERE c.session_id = u.session_id AND c.clock_id = u.clock_id)

rules.message: a unit's spikes carry an amplitude and the unit declares no amplitude_unit
rules.sql: SELECT DISTINCT u.unit_id FROM core.spike_events AS s JOIN core.units AS u USING (unit_id) WHERE s.amplitude IS NOT NULL AND u.amplitude_unit IS NULL
